text: Nearly every AI model you've used runs on one simple idea.
Matrix multiplication. And the chip built to do that math at scale is the T P U.
Meet Tiny T P U. A real four by four systolic array, written in SystemVerilog, that you can actually watch run.
Enter two small matrices, then press run.
The weights load into the grid and stay put. Matrix A streams in from the left, staggered on a diagonal.
Each cell multiplies, adds, and passes its partial sum down the column. One clock cycle at a time.
Nothing here is faked. This is the real hardware design, compiled to WebAssembly, running in your browser, and checked bit for bit against NumPy.
Play, pause, or step through every cycle, and scrub back in time whenever you like.
Then scale up. Large matrices tile across the same small array, one block at a time.
TinyTPU. A TPU you can watch run. It's open source, and you can try it right now.
